name: Global Product of Definite Integrals
description: Replaces the local $u \neq v$ inequality with a global constraint: the product of definite integrals over a strictly positive polynomial must be non-zero. The integral $\int_{u}^{v} (3t^2 - 2t + 1)dt$ evaluates to 0 if and only if $u=v$. By requiring the global product of these integrals across all links to be non-zero, the problem mathematically demands that $u \neq v$ for all given pairs. However, presenting it as a single global product obscures the independence of the conditions, tricking models into evaluating the constraint only on fully populated configurations. This prevents early pruning in backtracking and forces an $O(3^{40})$ Time Limit Exceeded, or causes logic failures if the model cannot symbolically evaluate the integral.
